name: AI Data-Centre Liquid Cooling: Fluids, Hoses & Heat Exchangers
scope: AI rack densities above 30 kW are pushing data centres from air to liquid cooling (IndexBox, Sep 2026: direct-to-chip ~18.5% CAGR and immersion fluids ~15% CAGR to 2035), and Indian listed small/mid caps are building capacity for coolant/dielectric fluids, liquid-cooling skids and hoses, and heat exchangers; partly discovered already (Aeroflex ~+123% in 6 months and KRN ~+130% off its 52-week low, both covered by retail finance media), while the fluids leg (Savita Oil, Apar) is earlier and less re-rated.
questions: What is data-centre liquid cooling (direct-to-chip, immersion, CDUs, manifolds, coolants/dielectric fluids) and why are AI rack densities forcing the shift, with the latest IndexBox/MarketsandMarkets/Mordor growth figures?
How big is India's data-centre build-out (announced hyperscale and AI capacity, MW pipeline) and what share of cooling content is likely to be liquid versus air over the next 3-5 years?
Which components and fluids in the liquid-cooling value chain are imported today versus made in India, and where is local content rising?

What exactly has Aeroflex Industries done (Rs 97.56 cr board-approved skid capacity expansion to 15,000 units, hose capacity additions, orders from a US-listed customer) and how concentrated/risky is its customer and tax-dispute position?

What are Savita Oil Technologies (QuantiCool coolants, Phase 2 synthetic ester plant commissioned 28 Feb 2026) and Apar Industries (Poweroil DC 10 immersion dielectric fluid) actually selling to data centres, and are revenues from this disclosed or still immaterial?

How real is KRN Heat Exchanger's data-centre exposure (Neemrana capacity, data-centre mix rising from 7% to 15%, hyperscale contract wins) and what does Blue Star's liquid-cooling effort amount to in filings and management commentary?

Are there other listed Indian names with company-confirmed liquid-cooling products or capex (cold plates, CDUs, quick-disconnect couplings, server OEMs such as Netweb) that qualify under the evidence bar?
How much has the market already priced in: stock performance over 3, 6 and 12 months for each name, valuation multiples, and the extent of broker and mainstream media coverage so far?
Which names are early (fluids, where data-centre revenue is a small slice) versus already re-rated (hoses and heat exchangers), and what is each company's data-centre revenue share?

What are the key risks (single-customer dependence, global OEM competition from Vertiv/Schneider, technology standard shifts, data-centre project delays, tax disputes) and what catalysts (quarterly orders, capacity commissioning dates, hyperscale announcements, PLI/policy support) are coming?

coolant_fluids: Glycol coolants and immersion/dielectric fluids for data-centre liquid cooling - the earliest, least re-rated leg
flow_components: Flexible hoses, liquid-cooling skids and fluid-handling assemblies inside racks and CDUs
heat_exchange_systems: Heat exchangers, chillers and integrated cooling systems for data-centre halls
